newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities steady to higher.

text.p: Singapore government securities were steady to slightly higher in moderate trade on Friday on retail and interbank interest, dealers said.

"The interbank rate eased slightly again today but there was still little impact on the market. Treasury bill yields and bond prices were steady to slightly higher. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months was unchanged from Thursday's yield of 2.95/2.90 percent but one-year closed at a yield of 2.80/2.75 percent compared with Thursday's yield of 2.79/2.74 percent.

Among bonds, April 1999 ended at S$98.53/98.58 against Thursday's close of S$98.48/98.53, September 2001 was unchanged from Thursday's close of S$96.30/96.40 and June 2003 ended at S$94.35/94.40 versus S$94.24/94.29.
The overnight interbank offered rate eased to 3-3/8 3-1/4 percent against Thursday's 3-9/16 3-7/16 percent.
